description: Compare irrigation pipe types, sizes, pressure ratings and public reference prices in Kenya. Check units carefully and request a current DripTech quotation.
intro: Irrigation pipe costs depend on material, diameter, pressure rating and the length supplied. This guide compares public supplier listings as a planning reference—not DripTech's own price list. Confirm current stock, exact specifications, delivery and tax before buying.

sections.heading: Public price references: compare like with like

title: Rain Hose Prices in Kenya: 32 mm, 40 mm & 50 mm | DripTech
description: Compare public rain hose price examples in Kenya by diameter and roll length, and learn what to check about flow, pressure and fittings.
intro: Rain hose distributes water through small perforations and can suit selected crops and field layouts. Prices depend on diameter, length, quality and accessories. The examples below are third-party public listings, not DripTech prices.

sections.heading: Public rain hose price examples
paragraphs: Grekkon's public page lists 100 m examples: 32 mm at KSh 2,500, 40 mm at KSh 5,800 and 50 mm at KSh 6,800. A separate Grekkon listing gives KSh 2,500, KSh 3,500 and KSh 4,500 for those sizes, so confirm the current price and exact product directly.
Check roll length, product specification, flow requirement, pressure/head conditions and whether connectors or end caps are included.

sections.heading: What to check before choosing rain hose
bullets: Diameter and flow required for crop and plot
Water source, pump capacity and available operating head
Hose length, perforation pattern and coverage
Connectors, end caps, valves and mainline pipe

sections.heading: Rain hose or drip irrigation?
paragraphs: Rain hose wets a broader area and may suit some short crops, nurseries and open-field layouts. Drip irrigation delivers water at emitters near the root zone and may be preferable where foliage wetting should be limited. The better option depends on crop, soil, water quality, wind, pressure and layout—not only initial roll price.

title: Button Drippers & Orchard Irrigation Kenya | DripTech
description: Plan orchard irrigation in Kenya with adjustable and pressure-compensating button drippers (4L/h, 8L/h), 16mm blind HDPE tubing and filtration.
h1: Button drippers and orchard irrigation systems in Kenya
intro: Fruit trees such as avocado, mango, citrus, macadamia and pawpaw are planted at wide spacing where pre-punched vegetable drip tape would waste water between trees. Button drippers mounted on 16 mm or 20 mm blind HDPE laterals deliver water directly to each tree basin.

sections.heading: Adjustable vs pressure-compensating (PC) button drippers
paragraphs: Adjustable button drippers allow farm operators to vary discharge at each tree from a gentle trickle up to higher flow as the canopy expands. Pressure-compensating (PC) button drippers (commonly 4 L/h or 8 L/h) maintain uniform discharge across sloping orchard blocks and long lateral runs.

table.caption: Comparing button dripper options for Kenyan orchards
rows: Flat to gentle plots, young-to-mature trees
Requires periodic manual balancing across zones
PC button dripper (4 L/h or 8 L/h)
Sloping land, undulating orchards & long rows
Maintains uniform flow within stated pressure range
Mature trees needing wider root-zone wetting
Higher flow rate per tree; size mainlines accordingly

sections.heading: Components of a complete orchard button-dripper system
bullets: Mainline and submain HDPE or uPVC pipes sized for total orchard zone flow
16 mm or 20 mm UV-stabilized blind PE lateral tubing laid along each tree row
2 to 4 button drippers per tree (or a ring loop around mature trunks) punched as roots expand
120-mesh screen or disc filter, air release valve, zone control valves and flush ends
Punch tool, goof plugs (for relocating emitters) and takeoff connectors with grommets

faqs.q: How many button drippers does one fruit tree need?
faqs.a: Young seedlings often start with 1 or 2 drippers near the root ball, expanding to 3 or 4 drippers arranged around the canopy drip line as the tree matures.

faqs.q: Why use blind HDPE pipe instead of pre-spaced dripline for orchards?
faqs.a: Trees spaced 4 m to 8 m apart only need water around each root zone. Blind pipe with button drippers avoids watering bare ground between trees where weeds would grow.

title: Pop-Up Lawn Sprinklers & Turf Irrigation Kenya | DripTech
description: Supply and installation of pop-up lawn sprinklers, gear-drive rotors, solenoid valves and automatic turf timers in Kenya from DripTech.
h1: Pop-up lawn sprinklers and landscape irrigation in Kenya
intro: Residential compounds, hotels, schools, sports pitches and commercial landscapes in Kenya use underground pop-up sprinklers and drip shrub lines for tidy, even watering without surface hoses.

sections.heading: Spray heads vs gear-drive rotor pop-up sprinklers
paragraphs: Fixed-arc or adjustable pop-up spray heads suit smaller lawn bays and curved garden beds with shorter throw radii. Gear-drive rotor pop-up sprinklers cover larger turf areas and sports fields at higher operating pressures.
Always design pop-up layouts for head-to-head coverage so the spray from one sprinkler reaches the base of the next sprinkler.
bullets: Group spray heads and gear-drive rotors on separate hydro-zones because their precipitation rates differ
Use shrub drip lines or micro-bubblers for flower beds, hedges and perimeter trees
Install automatic multi-station controllers, solenoid valve boxes and rain sensors for hands-free scheduling
Pressure-test underground HDPE/PVC pipework before backfilling lawn trenches

faqs.q: Can pop-up sprinklers run from normal domestic tank pressure?
faqs.a: Most pop-up spray heads and rotors require 2.0 to 3.5 bar of operating pressure, so an elevated tank alone is rarely sufficient without a booster pump.

faqs.q: Why should lawn sprinklers be spaced head-to-head?
faqs.a: Overlapping the throw radius from one sprinkler to the next prevents dry brown rings and uneven patches during windy or hot weather.

title: Rain Gun Sprinklers & Field Irrigation Kenya | DripTech
description: Compare rain gun sprinklers, tripod stands, high-pressure pumps and mainline pipe requirements for fodder, maize and pasture irrigation in Kenya.
h1: Rain gun sprinklers and large-area field irrigation in Kenya
intro: Rain gun sprinklers irrigate large blocks of fodder, pasture, maize, sugarcane and established field crops using a smaller number of movable or permanent hydrants. Because rain guns require substantial pressure and flow, the gun, pump and mainline must be engineered as one unit.

sections.heading: Matching rain gun nozzle size to pump pressure and flow
paragraphs: A rain gun will not break up its water jet into fine droplets if the pump pressure at the hydrant is too low. Operating a large rain gun on a low-head transfer pump produces a heavy stream that compacts soil and damages young crops.

table.caption: Key technical checks before buying a rain gun in Kenya
rows: Typically 2.5 to 5.0+ bar at the gun inlet
Controls throw radius and droplet breakup
Matches nozzle diameter and pump curve
Determines how many guns can run at once
PN10, PN12.5 or PN16 HDPE/PVC sized for low friction loss
Protects against pipe bursts and pressure drop
Avoid delicate flowering crops or high-wind afternoon runs

sections.heading: Complete rain gun kit components
bullets: Gear-drive or impact rain gun with interchangeable nozzle tips and adjustable sector arc
Galvanized tripod stand with quick-coupling hydrant valves and riser pipe
High-pressure centrifugal, diesel or solar-assisted booster pump
Heavy-duty delivery hose or layflat/HDPE mainline network

links.label: Request a rain gun system quote

faqs.q: Can one rain gun irrigate an entire acre from a single position?
faqs.a: Most farm rain guns are moved across 2 to 4 hydrant positions per acre depending on the model's wetted radius, operating pressure and required overlap.

faqs.q: Is a rain gun suitable for delicate vegetables like tomatoes or onions?
faqs.a: Drip irrigation or fine sprinklers are generally preferred for delicate vegetables and flowering crops, while rain guns excel on fodder, pasture, maize and pre-planting wetting.

title: Venturi Fertilizer Injectors & Fertigation Kenya | DripTech
description: Size and install 3/4", 1", 1.5" and 2" Venturi fertilizer injectors, bypass manifolds and soluble fertigation systems in Kenya with DripTech.
h1: Venturi fertilizer injectors and farm fertigation kits in Kenya
intro: A Venturi injector uses a pressure differential across a bypass manifold on your irrigation mainline to draw dissolved soluble fertilizer from a mixing tank directly into the irrigation water stream.

sections.heading: How to size and install a Venturi injector manifold
bullets: Match the Venturi size (3/4 inch, 1 inch, 1.5 inch or 2 inch) to the zone flow rate and available pump pressure
Install the injector on a parallel bypass assembly with a throttling gate or butterfly valve on the main line
Place a backflow preventer (check valve) upstream so fertilizer cannot siphon back into the water source
Install your primary disc or screen filter downstream (or use a suction strainer on the Venturi hose) so undissolved granules never reach drip emitters
Flush the drip lines with clean water for 10–15 minutes after every fertigation cycle

faqs.q: Why is my Venturi injector not sucking fertilizer from the tank?
faqs.a: Venturi injectors require a pressure differential between the inlet and outlet. Partially closing the bypass throttling valve on the mainline creates the pressure drop needed to start suction.

h1: Solenoid valves, water timers and automatic irrigation controllers in Kenya
intro: Automatic irrigation controllers and solenoid valves open and close irrigation zones on a programmed schedule, ensuring greenhouses, orchards and landscapes receive consistent water even when staff are away.

sections.heading: Choosing between tap timers, 9V DC battery controllers and 24V AC panels

table.caption: Irrigation controller and valve options in Kenya
rows: Kitchen gardens, balcony planters and small gravity tanks

sections.heading: Protecting solenoid valves from debris and pressure surges
bullets: Always install a screen or disc filter upstream of solenoid valves so sand or trash does not jam the diaphragm
Use waterproof gel-filled wire connectors inside underground valve boxes
Include a master valve or pump-start relay when the controller also starts an electric booster pump

faqs.q: Why won't a solenoid valve close completely after the timer finishes?
faqs.a: Small grit or leaf debris trapped under the rubber diaphragm or in the pilot port is the most common cause. Isolate the water, open the valve bonnet carefully and rinse the diaphragm.

title: uPVC Pressure Pipes & Fittings Kenya (PN6–PN16) | DripTech
description: Compare uPVC pressure pipes (PN6, PN10, PN12.5, PN16), solvent-weld/rubber-ring joints and HDPE transitions for Kenyan farm irrigation mainlines.
h1: uPVC pressure pipes and fittings for farm irrigation in Kenya
intro: Buried uPVC pressure pipes are widely used for permanent farm mainlines and submain headers in Kenya, often paired with HDPE risers and drip or sprinkler laterals above ground.

sections.heading: Understanding uPVC pressure classes (PN6, PN10, PN12.5 and PN16)
bullets: PN6 (6 bar): Low-pressure gravity mainlines and gentle submain headers
PN10 (10 bar): Standard pumped drip and medium-pressure farm mainlines
PN12.5 & PN16 (12.5–16 bar): High-head borehole delivery lines, steep uphill pumping and rain-gun mains
Bury uPVC pipes in stone-free trenches at least 45–60 cm deep so sunlight and farm tractors cannot damage them

links.label: Fix pipe leaks and fitting issues

faqs.q: Should I use uPVC or HDPE pipe for my irrigation mainline?
faqs.a: uPVC is economical for straight, buried permanent trenches in stable soil, while HDPE is preferred for surface lines, rocky trenches, curves and flexible connections.

faqs.q: How high should my water tank be for a gravity-fed 1/4 acre drip kit?
faqs.a: A tank stand raised at least 1.5 m to 3.0 m above the highest bed helps overcome filter and pipe friction losses for low-pressure gravity drip tape.
